# NSPanel HAUI 0.5.7

0.5.7 is about speed and size. The link to the display runs eight times faster, a page paints its own body colours instead of being handed 35 commands for them, an install no longer pushes its 11 MB display file over a link eight times slower than it needs to be, and the download an install fetches is about a fifth of what it was.

| | 0.5.6 | 0.5.7 |
|---|--------|-------|
| Display link | 115200 bps | **921600 bps** |
| An 11.5 MB TFT on the wire | ~17 min | **~2 min** |
| Commands to open a row panel | 141 | **117** |
| Commands to open a grid panel | 105 | **99** |
| Download of a HACS or Marketplace install | ~74 MB | **~15 MB** |

A faster link is also a link that can miss, so both ways it can go wrong are handled here: a panel still running the old TFT answers at 115200 and is found by the boot scan, and a display that cannot hold a transfer at 921600 gets the same install once more at the slow rate. The editor now names the link rate, so a panel that fell back to it is visible instead of only in the ESPHome log.

This release updates the integration, the editor and the firmware, and it carries new TFTs: display version **0.4.8** is required and arrives through the normal display update, after the firmware.

## Display link at 921600

Both TFTs boot the Nextion at 921600 bps instead of 115200 — the baud arrived with 0.4.6 and this release ships 0.4.8 — and the firmware starts its UART at the same rate. It still scans down for an older or stock TFT, so a panel flashed from another source keeps working, and the rate that answered is remembered so the next boot needs no scan.

A panel still running the 0.4.5 TFT answers at 115200. Its first boot after the firmware update waits for the display, power-cycles it and probes the Nextion rates until 115200 answers; that boot takes about 15 seconds. The display update that follows switches the TFT to 921600, and the first boot after that is about as long again while the firmware finds the new rate. Both boots finish on their own and later boots are immediate — leave the panel powered through them.

## What the faster link does to an install

An install pushes the panel's TFT to the display: 11.5 MB for landscape, 11.3 MB for portrait. At 115200 bps — 11,520 bytes a second — that file alone occupies the wire for about 17 minutes; at 921600 bps it is about 2 minutes. The UART stops being the floor under an install.

The transfer is not one stream, though: the panel hands the display 4 KB at a time and the display acknowledges every chunk, so the wall time also carries that handshake and the download. Expect an install to finish clearly faster than it used to, not in exactly an eighth of the time. The editor's progress estimate is unchanged at 15 minutes for a display install — an install that finishes well inside it is normal, and that quarter of an hour is the point past which the sidebar says the install is taking longer than usual.

A display that cannot hold the transfer at 921600 still gets its file; the **Fixed** list below says how.

## A page paints its own colours

A solid page already painted its backgrounds from the theme globals in `Program.s`; its body widgets kept the foreground colour compiled into them, which is the dark theme's, so the hub sent one `<widget>.pco=…` command per body widget with the panel's first render — 35 of them on the row page, 18 on the grid.

The TFT now declares those foregrounds as four more `Program.s` globals (`thmCompTxt`, `thmActive`, `thmActiveDk`, `thmTxt`) and stamps every body widget's foreground from them in its own Preinitialize code. The hub writes four globals before the page switch instead of one command per widget after it, so a row panel opens with 24 commands fewer (141 → 117 in the render the test suite replays, because an item's own state already repaints some of the same widgets) and a grid panel with 6 fewer (105 → 99). At the firmware's 2 ms command spacing that is roughly 50 ms off a row panel's first render, with no theme colour left to write per body widget afterwards.

Nothing breaks on a panel that has not had its display update yet: the switch is the version the display reports, and an older TFT keeps getting the colours from the hub exactly as before ([Design](docs/develop/design.md)).

## Smaller download

GitHub builds the source archive — the zip a HACS or Marketplace install downloads — from the repository, and `nextion/` carried ~59 MB of display sources and compiled TFTs that no install reads. That directory is now marked `export-ignore`, so the archive is about 15 MB instead of about 74 MB: a fifth of the download on every install and every update, which on a 16 Mbit/s connection is about 8 seconds instead of about 37.

Nothing else moves. Clones, the raw TFT URLs and the release assets are untouched, the integration that lands on disk is the same size either way, and git already delta-compresses successive HMI and TFT revisions, so a history rewrite would buy little ([Release process](docs/develop/release.md#guardrails-and-known-gaps)).

## Display file 0.4.8

The hub installs the 0.4.8 TFT only after the 0.5.7 firmware is running, because the firmware reports the display version it requires. That order is deliberate: an older firmware could not follow the display to 921600, and it would not write the four foreground globals, so a page on a light theme would paint dark-theme text until the hub sent its own. There is still one TFT per display model and nothing to choose.

## Before updating

Nothing. No renamed entity, no changed service, no migration. Update the integration first, then the firmware; the display follows on its own.

Expect the two slower first boots described under [Display link at 921600](#display-link-at-921600) — about 15 seconds each, longer when the display stays silent and the scan has to fall back to 115200 — and leave the panel powered through them. A panel that is still on the TFT's **Waiting for Initialization** page after a few minutes is recovered by another firmware update; [Troubleshooting](docs/user/troubleshooting.md#the-panel-stays-on-waiting-for-initialization-after-a-firmware-update) names the log lines to report if that does not help.

**If you build your own firmware**, one `ref:` is left to keep in step: the `packages:` remote package, which stays on `master` (or `dev` when you deliberately build the development branch). The vendored `nextion` patch now resolves from the directory that package was fetched into, so it can no longer disagree with the YAML beside it and no second ref can name another branch.

## Added

- **The display link in Diagnostics** — the **Versions** tile's details name the speed of the panel's link to its display, 921600 bps with a current TFT and lower after a fallback, and **Copy report** repeats it as a `Display link: … bps` line, so a slow link no longer needs the ESPHome log. A panel whose Nextion has never answered reports **Unknown** rather than the 115200 bps it falls back to, so a broken link does not read as a working slow one ([Editor](docs/user/editor/README.md)).
- **Logs in the device's side stack** — the Device screen opens **Logs** for the device shown, between **Themes** and **Updates**, so one device's lines no longer need the fleet overview ([Editor](docs/user/editor/README.md)).

## Changed

- **The display link runs at 921600 bps** — both TFTs boot the Nextion there and the firmware starts its UART at the same rate, scanning down only for an older or stock TFT; there is still one TFT per display model, and existing panels get the faster link with their next display update ([Display baud](docs/develop/nextion.md#display-baud)).
- **A page paints its body foregrounds itself** — the TFT declares them as four `Program.s` globals and stamps each body widget's foreground in Preinitialize, so the hub sends four colour globals instead of one command per body widget: a row panel opens with 24 commands fewer, a grid panel with 6 fewer. An older TFT keeps the hub's per-widget colours ([Design](docs/develop/design.md)).
- **An install downloads a fifth as much** — `nextion/` is out of GitHub's source archives, so a HACS or Marketplace install fetches about 15 MB instead of about 74 MB; clones, the raw TFT URLs and the release assets are unchanged ([Release process](docs/develop/release.md#guardrails-and-known-gaps)).
- **`dev` is the integration branch again** — `master` stays stable-only and is the repository default, so a clone and any link without a ref read released code while a **Development** firmware build carries unreleased code; a stable release still arrives through a promotion pull request and a `vX.Y.Z` tag ([Release process](docs/develop/release.md)).
- **A failure on the Fleet screen reads as a banner** — a **Scan** that failed and a **Device status could not be refreshed** notice sit in a tinted banner above **Device inventory** with a glyph that repeats the message, instead of a line of red text under the device carousel. The failed scan is still announced at once and the stale status politely, and the tone no longer carries the meaning alone ([Editor](docs/user/editor/README.md)).
- **The Device screen's action buttons fit a narrow screen** — **Themes**, **Logs**, **Updates** and **Backups** take two per line below 980px and one row of icon tiles on a phone, where the value each one showed takes no room and stays in its name for a screen reader ([Editor](docs/user/editor/README.md)).
- **The Fleet inventory header survives a phone** — its title and device count stay visible, with update and integration-version labels beside their values in a compact two-column strip instead of crowding the header's right edge, and the card ends with its device table: the bar of one coloured segment per device and its hover tip are gone, since every row already carries its device's connection icon and a selected row names it ([Editor](docs/user/editor/README.md)).
- **A card reads title band, then content** — every card heading now sits on the soft surface, one step above its body: **Device inventory**, **Latest events** and **Discovered Devices** on Fleet, the Device screen's workspace strip and its side cards, a sidebar's title strip and the panel groups inside it ([Editor](docs/user/editor/README.md)).

## Fixed

- **A silent display is recovered** — the boot scan no longer gives up for the rest of the boot. Each probe re-enables the display's command returns first, because a display that was just power-cycled is back on its power-on defaults and answers no `get` without them; a scan that finds nothing leaves the link at 115200 instead of at the rate nothing answered at, and the scan runs three more times a minute apart. A panel that sat on the TFT's **Waiting for Initialization** page is brought back by a firmware update in the meantime ([Display baud](docs/develop/esphome.md#display-baud)).
- **A slow display still gets its TFT** — an install the display itself fails at 921600 is retried once at 115200 bps. The panel power-cycles the display first, because a failed transfer leaves it waiting for data, and reports the install as failed only when the retry fails too. A download, range or heap error is not retried: another transfer at any rate would end the same way ([Troubleshooting](docs/user/troubleshooting.md#the-panel-refuses-every-tft-upload)).
- **The fallback survives the retries** — a retry waits at whatever the last scan settled on instead of switching back to the rate that answered nothing, so the 115200 bps fallback gets the window it exists for ([Display baud](docs/develop/esphome.md#display-baud)).
- **Self-built firmware compiles its own patch** — the vendored `nextion` patch comes from the directory the package was fetched into, not from `master`, so a **Development** build compiles the patch that belongs to `dev` (it used to stop at `no member named 'tft_upload_display_fault'`) and a stale component cache cannot pair a new display config with an older patch ([Troubleshooting](docs/user/troubleshooting.md#esphome-stops-with-couldnt-find-remote-ref)).
- **Hardware buttons run the domain's own action** — a button assigned a scene, script, button, lock, vacuum or input select sends that domain's action instead of a `toggle` the domain does not provide, so a scene on a hardware button with its relay off activates instead of failing with a Home Assistant service error ([Hardware buttons](docs/user/editor/device.md#hardware-buttons)).
- **A grid tile's power button does too** — `turn_on`/`turn_off` go only to a domain that has them, and a scene, script, button, lock, vacuum or input select runs its own action, so a lock tile's power button locks and unlocks instead of failing with a Home Assistant service error ([Grid](docs/user/panels/panel_grid.md#colors)).
- **A reading stays on its label's line** — the tile card fits the widest translation's label beside a reading such as **921600 bps**, and a label that still does not fit wraps instead of pushing the reading onto a line of its own, so **Diagnostics → Versions** shows **Display link** on one line ([Editor](docs/user/editor/README.md)).
- **One version-check line per check** — the TFT check logs `Checking installed version` once instead of twice when the display has already reported its version, so the line whose `installed=` is empty is the only one that means the display told the hub nothing ([Troubleshooting](docs/user/troubleshooting.md#the-panel-refuses-every-tft-upload)).
